source_title: Building on ACP at OpenClaw — Agent-Client Protocol and Orchestration (Honor Solaz, Text Cortex / OpenClaw maintainer)
speaker: Honor Solaz
speaker_affiliation: Founding Engineer at Text Cortex; OpenClaw maintainer (day-one); ACPX author; MS Teams integration contributor
key_insight: ACP (Zed's Agent-Client Protocol) + ACPX CLI as the protocol substrate for standardized agent-to-agent handoff; SOPs-for-agents ('automating the automator') as the scaling pattern once PR volume explodes; Spritz (Text Cortex open-source Go K8s operator) as the enterprise dispatch template for on-demand disposable agents.

discovered_urls.context: Agent-Client Protocol (ACP) spec and reference implementation from Zed — the foundation Honor built ACPX on top of. Standardizes how a host client (editor, chat, IDE, CLI) talks to an agent. Explicitly NOT MCP (which is agent-to-tool).
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: Direct candidate to replace our ad-hoc tmux send-keys worker handoff with a protocol-native layer. Compatible with Codex, Claude Code, and OpenClaw via Zed's existing adapters.

discovered_urls.context: Zed editor's agent panel documentation — the canonical ACP host implementation, showing how a client drives an ACP-compliant agent
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: Reference implementation of ACP client side; useful for understanding what our orchestrator would need to implement if we became an ACP client

discovered_urls.context: ACPX — Honor's Swiss-army-knife CLI that wraps ACP and lets any agent call any other agent over command line. Also supports Codex app-server protocol (contributed by Herald). Repo URL is inferred from Text Cortex org + project name; needs verification.
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: Candidate replacement for our tmux-based worker handoff. Lets our orchestrator call Codex/Claude Code/OpenClaw through one uniform protocol. Also positioned as general-purpose workflow engine with structured JSON output — could encode our review/fix loop SOP.

discovered_urls.context: Spritz — Text Cortex's open-source Go Kubernetes operator for on-demand disposable dispatchable agents. Concierge agent on Slack spawns task-specific agents in full K8s pods backed by Firecracker microVMs. Currently used for error reporting at Text Cortex. Repo URL is inferred; needs verification.
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: Template for enterprise-tier orchestrator deployment. If we scale past one client running in parallel, this is the pattern we'd copy rather than invent: concierge on chat → dispatch agent per task → user gets a link to the fresh session.

discovered_urls.context: Text Cortex company site — Honor's employer; builder of the Ship-of-Theseus production harness (started 2022 as Jupyter Lab extension over OG Codex/Davinci-Code-2) and Spritz
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: Peer startup in the coding harness space; reference for personal-to-enterprise agent spectrum framing

discovered_urls.context: OpenClaw main repo — Honor is a day-one maintainer. Context for the PR firehose anecdote (60K+ PRs, 300-500/day, 90% AI slop) that motivated the SOP tooling work
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: Already catalogued. This talk adds interop-layer detail (ACP adapter, Discord/Telegram bridges) that should refresh the existing entry

discovered_urls.context: OpenAI Codex — the 'reliable coder' end of Honor's telephone game (Opus → Codex via CLI when Opus was unreliable for complex coding). Target of Honor's ACP adapter via ACPX.
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: Already referenced in other catalogue entries; this talk confirms Codex as the interop target for ACPX

discovered_urls.context: Zed editor (Rust) — originator of ACP; shipped Codex and Claude Code adapters first, which is why Honor chose ACP over the competing Agent Protocol
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: Reference for why ACP won the adapter race; Zed is worth tracking as a peer host implementation

discovered_urls.context: Firecracker microVMs — the isolation layer Spritz uses under its Kubernetes pods for dispatchable agent sessions
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: Candidate isolation primitive if we move beyond tmux workers to true per-agent VMs

discovered_urls.context: Peter Steinberger's blog — home of the 'Cloud Code is my computer' article Honor cites as the founding text of this whole thread of work
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: Historical reference for the OpenClaw origin story; worth ingesting the founding article

action_items: Evaluate ACPX as a protocol-native replacement for our tmux send-keys worker handoff layer
Add ACPX, ACP, and Spritz as tool/protocol catalogue entries once repo URLs are confirmed
Encode our orchestrator's review/fix loop as an explicit SOP matching Honor's abstract workflow (intent → judge → conflicts → CI → review → make CI pass); store as .bmad/sops/review-fix-loop.yaml
Track Agent Protocol vs ACP adoption over the next 6 months — winner decides the agent interop standard
Cross-reference with State of the Claw (same conference) for the PR firehose context from Peter Steinberger's platform-level view
Cross-reference with Ryan Lopopolo's harness engineering talk — SOPs-for-agents is a direct parallel to his 'prompts as lint' framing
